Process_Text.original: The heat treatment process was as follows: heating to 850 °C and holding for 2 h, quenching in oil, and tempering at 180 °C for 4 h, according to the ISO 683–17 standard. The grinding experiment was performed on a precision horizontal axis surface grinding machine (MGK 7120 × 6, Hangzhou Machine Tool Co., Ltd., China). A resin-bonded CBN grinding wheel was employed. The experimental conditions were dry grinding, and the grinding process was completed in one pass. The grinding depth was set to 40 μm, and the speeds of the grinding wheel and worktable were maintained at 31.4 m/s and 0.1 m/s, respectively.
Process_Text.simplified: AISI 52100 steel quenched (850°C/2h/oil) and tempered (180°C/4h), then surface ground in one pass under dry conditions at depth 40 μm, wheel speed 31.4 m/s, worktable speed 0.1 m/s.

Wheel_Runout.Note: Inequality value: circular runout reduced to less than 1 μm after dressing

Structure_Text.original: The microstructures of the heat-treated workpiece were composed of tempered martensite, spherical carbides, tempered carbides, and a small amount of residual austenite. After grinding, the ground surface cross-section shows a white layer and a dark layer. The white layer microstructure is greatly refined, tightly bonded, with flat and smooth morphology. At the top surface, cryptocrystalline region (3 μm depth) and rheological region (10 μm depth) exist. The white layer is predominantly acicular martensite with some elongated carbide particles and few corrosion pits. SAED pattern near ground surface shows α-BCC martensite and γ-FCC austenite, no ε or θ carbides detected. Nanocrystalline layer near ground surface with grain sizes 10-50 nm. At 6 μm depth: lamellar grains tilted/elongated with dislocation tangles and dislocation walls. At 3 μm depth: elongated lamellar grains split into dislocation cells. At 2 μm depth: nanoscale subgrains with strong texture. At 1 μm depth: mixed columnar and equiaxed nanocrystals. Near ground surface: equiaxed α-BCC nanocrystals with 20 nm recrystallization nuclei. Fe₃C carbide particles retained at various depths with HCP structure.
Structure_Text.simplified: Pre-grinding: tempered martensite + spherical carbides + tempered carbides + residual austenite. After grinding: white layer (surface, acicular martensite + retained austenite, carbide-depleted, nanocrystalline at top) and dark layer (subsurface, over-tempered martensite + ferrite, carbide-enriched). White layer shows depth-dependent grain refinement from DRV to cDRX+dDRX, grain sizes 10-50 nm near surface. Fe₃C (HCP) carbide particles retained undissolved at various depths.

Main_Phase.Note: Acicular martensite dominant in white layer; formed by re-austenitization followed by rapid cooling

Volume_Fraction.Note: Austenite volume fraction in white layer from XRD analysis

Secondary_Phases.Note: Retained microscale spherical carbides undissolved during grinding due to short contact duration. Reduced content compared to bulk. Fe₃C confirmed HCP by IFFT at 2 μm depth.

White_Layer_Thickness.Note: White layer thickness not explicitly stated as a single number; cryptocrystalline region ~3 μm, rheological region ~10 μm from top surface

Dark_Layer_Depth.Note: Dark layer extends below white layer; exact boundary not given as a single numerical value

LAGB_Fraction_White_Layer.Note: Low-angle grain boundaries (2°-15° misorientation) in white layer from EBSD

Texture_or_Orientation.Preferential_Orientation: No preferential orientation in white layer or dark layer (from EBSD IPF maps)

Depth_Profile.Characteristics: Lamellar grains tilted and elongated along grinding depth; high-density dislocation tangles (DTs); dislocation pile-ups forming dislocation walls (DWs); dislocation steps (DSs) formed
Elongated lamellar grains split into dislocation cells (DCs); dislocation annihilation and rearrangement near dislocation walls and steps; SAED shows discontinuous arc-shaped bright spots

Nanoscale subgrains with strong texture; dislocation cells evolved into subgrains; Fe₃C carbide particles with HCP structure confirmed by IFFT; twisted nanocrystal ~30 nm diameter at two-phase interface

Mixed columnar and equiaxed nanocrystals; columnar nanocrystals with nearly identical long-axis direction and parallel grain alignments; equiaxed nanocrystals arranged in chain-like manner; evidence of dDRX
Equiaxed α-BCC nanocrystals with regular morphology and low dislocation density; 20 nm recrystallization nuclei; SAED shows continuous ring pattern; grain sizes 10-50 nm; evidence of cDRX

Austenite_Volume_Fraction_White_Layer.Note: From XRD; increased from 8.4% in bulk due to grinding-induced re-austenitization

Grinding_Peak_Temperature.Note: Peak grinding temperature, exceeded Ac_cm critical point (900 °C) for complete austenitization

Cooling_Rate.Note: From peak temperature to Ms (200 °C) during 0.3-0.75 s

Carbide_Size_At_Interface.Note: Twisted nanocrystal at stress concentration area near carbide-matrix interface at 2 μm depth

Surface_Integrity.Nanocrystallization_Mechanism: Grain refinement progressed from dynamic recovery (DRV) to predominantly continuous dynamic recrystallization (cDRX) with minor discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (dDRX). Carbide particles exerted pinning effect promoting dislocation multiplication and cross-slip.

Test_Condition.Measurement_Method: Vickers microhardness, interlaced measurement, 10 μm depth interval, 30 μm horizontal spacing

Properties.Note: Peak hardness in white layer; hardness distributed in gradient manner (higher closer to surface). Error bars represent 1 STDEV (n=3).
Approximately 25 N/mm; approximate value explicitly stated in text
Approximately 10 N/mm; approximate value explicitly stated in text

Process_Text.original: The subsurface experienced a slower cooling rate and longer holding time after grinding, and the temperature was not high enough for re-austenitization. As a result, the material underwent high-temperature tempering.
Process_Text.simplified: Dark layer formed by grinding-induced high-temperature tempering of subsurface where temperature remained below Ac_cm; slower cooling and longer hold time than surface.

Thermal_Condition.Temperature_Range: Below Ac_cm (900 °C) but sufficient for high-temperature tempering
Thermal_Condition.Note: No austenite transformation; no austenite peaks detected in XRD

Processing.Note: Grinding equipment and pre-grinding heat treatment shared with Item1 (same workpiece). Equipment for characterization listed in Item1.

Structure_Text.original: The dark layer exhibited severe etching, as evidenced by its rough morphology with numerous irregular corrosion grooves. The density of carbide particles in the dark layer was higher than that of the bulk material, but the average particle size remained smaller than that of the bulk material. The dark layer showed contrast differences indicating carbon-depleted and carbon-enriched areas. XRD shows no austenite peaks. Martensite peaks were intensified and narrowed, indicating weakened lattice distortion. EBSD shows improved band contrast, fewer defects, reduced lattice distortions, and more regular grain boundaries compared to white layer. LAGB fraction 15.9%. KAM map shows low and uniformly distributed dislocation density.
Structure_Text.simplified: Dark layer: over-tempered martensite + ferrite, carbide-enriched, carbon segregation areas, no retained austenite, weakened lattice distortion, low dislocation density.

Main_Phase.Note: Dark layer consists of over-tempered martensite and ferrite composites; c/a ratio of α-Fe lattice restored to 1

Secondary_Phases.Note: Significant amount of cementite precipitated along dislocation lines and grain boundaries; higher carbide content than bulk material and white layer

LAGB_Fraction_Dark_Layer.Note: Lower than white layer (37.7%) and bulk (21.9%); indicates subgrain coalescence and boundary annihilation

Austenite_Volume_Fraction_Dark_Layer.Note: No austenite peaks detected in XRD diffraction pattern of dark layer

Properties.Note: Minimum hardness in dark layer; approximately 70% of bulk material hardness (740 HV)

The bulk material contained a large amount of lathy martensite and a small amount of acicular martensite. EBSD shows intermediate dislocation characteristics between white and dark layers.
